issue.body:
How much validation coverage is lost through test recognition, command selection and output parsing? Follow-up to #28; investigation remains open.

**Live targeting result:** a general selector excluding deleted test paths removes Matchms PR958's missing-file error, but both stages then stop during collection because historical code imports missing `chemap`. No task is recovered. PR671 preserves exact native sets under both selections: 1 fail-to-pass and 30 pass-to-pass tests. Transport, validator/parser, source/test patches and reconstructed image were held fixed; no dependency repair was applied.

**Other findings:** four of six predeclared SAMtools PRs add net Perl test invocations, while the pinned recognizer counts zero for all six. SGR normalization passes 12 fixtures in both native and exported parsers. The original outer-only completion candidate is insufficient: actual shell execution can hide inner test failures behind outer exit 0. MNE's explicit broad target remains a separate selection issue.

**Completion candidate:** a separate pytest-specific gate preserves inner exits, fails on native setup errors and prevents exported reward from interrupted runs. Six real pytest/Bash/Git fixture cases and five standalone-export checks pass: expected nop/oracle remain 0/1; partial error credit changes 0.5→0. This is synthetic-repository evidence, not biological recovery. [Checks and limitations](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/ae0ef75b/experiments/32-runner-coverage/pytest-completion-protocol.md).

**Remaining:** evaluate general runner support and MNE targeting, then exercise the revised parser/completion candidate on frozen live cases. Any recovery claim requires complete positive controls. No per-PR command/dependency edits or additional LLM repair loop.

**Execution:** one live job, one attempt, 0.22337 allocated CPU-hours against a 10-hour ceiling, zero model calls. Owned resources are removed and archive readback verified. Raw Matchms evidence stays private; reconstruction drift limits historical equivalence. No exports or independent Harbor controls were generated by this comparison.

[Live diagnosis](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/40a80ef0/experiments/32-runner-coverage/target-live-diagnosis.json) · [Archive/cleanup verification](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/40a80ef0/experiments/32-runner-coverage/live-readback.json) · [Selection checks](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/40a80ef0/experiments/32-runner-coverage/deleted-target-results.json) · [Full scope](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/40a80ef0/experiments/32-runner-coverage/issue-scope.md). Detailed logs remain in comments.

comment_body:
🤖 **The outer-only completion gate was insufficient.** Actual Bash/Git fixtures showed that upstream and that candidate can accept parseable F2P/P2P-shaped output after the inner test command exits 2, 124 or 137: the final marker echo hides the test status behind outer exit 0. The earlier seven synthetic checks cover outer failures/missing markers only and are preserved. [Counterexample](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/ffa89674/experiments/32-runner-coverage/inner-exit-diagnosis.md).

A separate explicit-pytest candidate now fails closed on native setup errors, preserves the inner test exit, requires ordered newline-separated markers, and applies a compatible exit gate before exported reward. It combines the same SGR normalization in native/export parsers. Six real pytest/Bash/Git native fixture cases and five standalone-export cases pass: expected nop/oracle remain 0/1; keyboard interruption, explicit exit124 and SIGKILL change from prior SGR-only partial reward 0.5 to 0. Per-test IDs are preserved. Additional checks reject malformed markers and explicitly skip unsupported runners. [Results](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/ae0ef75b/experiments/32-runner-coverage/pytest-completion-results.json) · [Protocol and limitations](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/ae0ef75b/experiments/32-runner-coverage/pytest-completion-protocol.md).

These are actual local executions of a small synthetic repository, not biological recovery, a full Harbor run or regrading of any original result. Strict native completion currently supports explicit pytest commands only; arbitrary wrappers can still mask their own exits, and exported reset behavior remains separate #31 work. The initial fixture Git-config failure and the discovered missing-newline protocol failure are retained; the final check passed in 2.46 seconds at 43,824 KiB peak RSS with temporary storage removed. Zero model calls and no additional remote job. Live frozen-case comparison and broader runner support remain open.
